# SP2 Core Pages Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Rebuild the seven core pages (Home, Agents, Runs, Team Room, Workspace, Setup, Safety) in the approved Cobalt design, on real data. Ship with them the three behaviour changes the spec puts in SP2: the Team Room asks before saving (D10), Setup never answers an updater's question for the user, and Workspace shows who saved each file.

**Architecture:** One shared page kit (`PageHeader`, `Banner`, `Tabs`, `Meter`, `EmptyState`, `StatusWord` and table classes in `src/ui/kit.css`) is built first. Every page task then rebuilds one page on that kit and the SP1 tokens, keeping its existing API calls. Server changes are test-first in the existing `node --test` suite. Every UI task adds a probe to the git-ignored audit harness (`.superpowers/ui-audit/`) and is compared by eye with the prototype screenshots.

**Tech Stack:** React 18 + Vite + TypeScript (UI), Node (≥ 18; the desktop app bundles its own) + Express 4 (server), `node --test` (tests), lucide-react (icons), the SP1 Cobalt tokens (`src/ui/tokens.css`), a Playwright-core audit harness against a throwaway server with fake agents.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-cobalt-redesign-and-real-terminals-design.md`, section "SP2 Core pages" (with D10, D11 and D13). The spec is binding; this plan argues from it.

**Prototype (owner-approved, the visual target):** `~/MediaStudio/runs/2026-10-10-agent-os-redesign/prototype/` (`<page>.html`, `shared/cobalt.css`, `kit.html`, `shots/*.png`). Build to match it with real data, never its sample data. To view it live: `cd ~/MediaStudio/runs/2026-10-10-agent-os-redesign/prototype && python3 -m http.server 4610 --bind 127.0.0.1`.

**Builds on:** SP1 (done and pushed: `d0e5716..32b6879`). The SP1 ledger, with rulings R1–R17 and deferred minors, is at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-11-sp1-design-system-and-shell/progress.md`.

## Global Constraints

- **Tokens:** only the tokens in `src/ui/tokens.css`. No new colour literals. Move the remaining old amber/red/green `rgba(...)` status colours in the page CSS you touch onto `--os-ok/--os-warn/--os-danger` (+ `-wash`, `-line`).
- **One accent:** cobalt `#3866EE` is for the primary action, the live state and the focus ring only. Small cobalt text uses `--os-accent-strong`. Status is always an icon plus a word, never colour alone.
- **Box-shadow order:** when an element has both an accent ring and an elevation, the accent ring comes first: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--os-accent-line), var(--os-e2);`.
- **Motion:** 120–200 ms with `var(--os-ease-out)`, and everything is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. No count-up animations, glows, grain or decorative gradients. No coloured left borders thicker than 1 px; draw a coloured tab as a shape.
- **Fonts:** Archivo for the UI. JetBrains Mono (`.os-mono`) for data only: ids, versions, paths, counts, model names.
- **Breakpoints (unchanged):**
  - off-canvas menu at ≤ 900 px;
  - 64 px icon rail from 901 to 1366 px (D13; the prototype pictures at 1280 px show the full sidebar, so judge 1280 with the rail);
  - full 228 px sidebar at ≥ 1367 px.
  - Window minimum is 1024×640. No sideways scroll at any width.
- **Copy:**
  - plain English, sentence case;
  - `.os-micro` captions are never typed in capitals;
  - no em dash in visible text;
  - "—" means unknown and "…" means loading;
  - empty, error and offline states are designed, never blank;
  - the menu names are the page names (Home, not Fleet; "Dry-run chat", not Chat).
- **D11:** no UI text may say that Hold to stop all stops the Hermes background service or the OpenClaw Gateway. It stops agent work: runs now, and sessions from SP3. Each service has its own Stop on Agents.
- **D10:** agreement between agents never writes a file. Only the person's Approve does.
- **Legacy:** core pages use no `aos-*` class and no `PageFrame` after SP2. `src/styles.css`, `src/agent-os.css` and `src/phase2.css` are not edited or deleted, because Labs pages use them.
- **Inventory behaviours that must keep working:**
  - ⌘K/Ctrl+K palette focus trap and restore;
  - Escape closes the menu or rail and returns focus;
  - `aria-current="page"`;
  - the rail tooltip `role="tooltip"`;
  - the `#os-get-started` focus target;
  - `data-density` on `<html>`;
  - 5 s polling through `useInterval` (pauses on a hidden tab);
  - modal titles `os-modal-title` / `os-setup-modal-title`;
  - no `position: fixed` control inside ModelPicker;
  - `.os-run-console__transcript` and the setup log (`role="log"`, scroll-follow) stay the scroll containers;
  - the `test/release-config.test.js` window minimums.
- **Placeholders until later (spec):**
  - Home's waiting strip and Safety's waiting rows show their designed empty state until SP4.
  - Home's "New session" and the Agents header's "Open session" / "New session" stay hidden until SP3.
  - Runs' Session recordings tab shows a designed empty state until SP3.
- **Workers:**
  - never commit, push, tag or set `CI=true`;
  - never start a real agent (fakes only, temp `HOME`/`AGENT_OS_HOME`);
  - never read `.env` files or the `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.openclaw` or `~/.hermes` credential files;
  - retry until the listed checks are green;
  - report anything that could not be done.
- **Installing packages needs the owner's OK first.** The only candidate in SP2 is `tauri-plugin-opener` for "Show in Finder" (Task B3 asks).
- **Audit harness:** run `node .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs <mode>`, or `… probe .superpowers/ui-audit/probes/<name>.mjs`, from the worktree root. It starts a throwaway server on :8791 with fake agents and a temp HOME. Run one at a time, and make sure nothing is left on :8791 afterwards. Playwright-core is borrowed from `~/.npm/_npx/a80a913f4f8f2557` (override with `PLAYWRIGHT_CORE=<path>`).

## Review Focus

The five situations a person will meet that the spec implies but no task's main tests exercise, most likely first. Each one has a test in the task named after it.

1. **Agent OS quits or restarts while a Team Room is paused for a decision.** After restart the room must still read "Paused for your decision", with `pausedFor` set and the clock still stopped at `clockUsedMs`. It must not resume, expire or lose the proposal. (Task A1)
2. **The same decision arrives twice, or Approve and Continue land together.** For example a double click, or two windows. The file is written once, the room resumes once, and the second request gets a clear "already decided" answer. (Task A2)
3. **A Workspace file whose Team Room history is gone.** The room was deleted, its actions log is missing or corrupt, or the person overwrote the file after an agent saved it. "Saved by" shows the honest value ("—", or "Changed outside Agent OS" after an edit), "Undo this save" is not offered, the server's Undo refuses rather than throw the edit away, and nothing crashes. (Tasks A4, B2 and B3)
4. **Starting a run when it cannot run.** The safety level is Look only, the execution gate is off, the agent is not installed, or the task is empty. The New run dialog says why in plain words and points to the fix (Safety, Setup), instead of failing silently or showing a raw error. (Task C3)
5. **Agent OS unreachable, or an agent missing, while a page is open.** Home, Agents, Runs and Safety show their designed offline or "Not installed" state with "—" values. No spinner runs forever, and the page recovers on its own when the server comes back (5 s polling). (Tasks C2, C3, D1, D2)

## Decisions taken while planning (the owner can overturn any of these)

The spec is silent on these points, or the drafts raised them. Each was decided as follows, and the tasks already follow the decision.

| # | Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | A room paused on its very last allowed turn: what happens after the decision? | Approve saves the file and ends the room `agreed`. Reject ends it `needs_you`, and Continue can add turns. There is no automatic extra turn. | Spec item 4: "resumes the room with the turns it has left (no extra turns)". |
| P2 | Is Stop offered on a paused room? | No. A paused room is not running, so the server's Stop answers 409. The page offers the decision card and Continue instead. | Matches the server, and avoids a button that cannot work. |
| P3 | What if the person decides while the room cannot resume (gate off, another room running, an agent not ready)? | The decision is saved and the pause ends. The room stays `needs_you`, with a plain reason saying the decision is saved and what to do, and Continue is offered. | Spec item 4: "otherwise the decision is recorded and the room stays `needs_you` with Continue offered". |
| P4 | The spec lists nine Team Room tests to rewrite. | Ten are rewritten. "undo: refuses when the recorded path no longer matches the room" also fails as written. | It reads an action that, after D10, only exists after an Approve. |
| P5 | After a decision resumes a room, what does the page's clock show? | The server rewinds `clockStartedAt` by the time already used, so the page's clock (`now - clockStartedAt`) and the server's limit agree. A test pins it. | Otherwise the Time meter would restart at 0 while the limit kept counting. |
| P6 | How are the agents told about the decision? | Only a decision that ended a pause is reported, once, in each agent's next prompt (or after a later Continue). Decisions on other cards stay silent, as today. | Spec item 4 ("the next turn's prompt tells the agents the decision"), without repeating it every turn. |
| P7 | Approve, but a link is where the file should go (the save is refused). | This counts as a decision. The pause ends, the room resumes, and the agents are told "approved, but the file could not be saved". | The person decided. The refusal is reported honestly, and the room is not stuck. |
| P8 | Files Agent OS writes itself, other than the welcome note (the mission note, exports): what does "Saved by" say? | "—" in SP2, as the spec names only the welcome note. Marking them "Agent OS" is a small follow-up. | Keeps SP2 inside the spec. "—" is honest. |
| P9 | The Team Room's own Undo would throw away an edit the person made after the agent's save. | The server refuses: 409 `changed_since_save`, nothing changed (new Task A4, test-first). | Never lose the person's work. Hiding the Workspace button alone was not enough. |
| P10 | A Team Room file changed after the agent saved it: does "Saved by" say "You"? | No. It says "Changed outside Agent OS" (kind `unknown`), with no Undo. "You" means only a note saved through Agent OS's own form. | Agent OS cannot tell who changed it (the person, an editor, another program), so it does not guess. |
| P11 | With `--yes` removed, an OpenClaw update that asks a question now fails with the updater's own message. Ship before spike S5? | Yes. | The spec intends exactly this (SP2 Setup row; S5 checks it later). Answering a question for the person is the risk being removed. |
| P12 | Show "agreed by Hermes and OpenClaw, approved by you" on Workspace files? | Not in SP2. The page shows "Team Room · <agent who proposed it>". | The prototype's meta line says "Saved by Team Room". The extra line is optional polish. |
| P13 | Keep a "Continue without deciding (+4 turns)" button on a paused room? | Yes, as a secondary button. | Spec item 5 lets Continue accept a paused room. Without it, a person whose execution gate is off has no way to keep the room moving. |
| P14 | The Team Room logic test needs TypeScript helpers. Add `esbuild` as a dependency? | No. The test imports the `.ts` file directly: Node strips the types (≥ 22.18 here, 24 in CI). The helper file must keep `import type` only. | No new dependency, and nothing to install. |
| P15 | Team Room limits: the prototype shows drop-downs, today's page has number fields. | Number fields, styled like the prototype's fields. | The server accepts any value in its ranges (turns 2–12, minutes 1–30, optional cost cap), and the fields already validate. Reported to the owner as a deliberate difference. |
| P16 | Team Room turns: time of day, or time since the room started (the prototype)? | Time of day. | A pause makes "time since start" wrong. Time of day is always true. |
| P17 | Team Room agent lines: the prototype shows the maker and the brain or model. | The maker names are fixed facts (Hermes: Nous Research; OpenClaw: open source). The brain line becomes the installed version, with a pointer to Agents. | There is no cheap per-room API for the brain. A wrong brain line would be worse than none. |
| P18 | The "no `aos-` on core pages" check also matches the `aos-navigate` event name. | The check excludes `aos-navigate`. It is the page-change event in `src/nav.ts`, not a class. | It keeps the check meaningful without renaming a shared event. |
| P19 | `npm test` runs every `*.test.js` under the worktree, including git-ignored folders. | Plan drafts and scratch folders never contain `*.test.js` files. E1 runs the full suite only on a clean tree. | A copied test file in a scratch folder would otherwise run against stale code. |
| P20 | Workspace's "Copy path" and "Show in Finder" need the real folder path, which other responses hide on purpose. | `GET /api/workspace` adds `roots[].absolutePath` in the local app only. It stays `null` on the public demo. | The person's own app showing the person's own path is fine. The public demo still shows none. |
| P21 | New Workspace notes: today they go to `notes/`; the prototype's sample shows `inbox/`. | Keep `notes/`. | Other pages link into the existing folders. Moving them is a change with no benefit to the person. |
| P22 | The core pages render `<section>`s, so the app has no `main` region for screen readers. | The shell's content area gets `role="main"` on core pages only (Task D3). Labs pages keep their own `<main>`, so there is never more than one. | One main landmark per page, without touching the Labs pages. |
| P23 | Setup's AI brain step: the prototype draws one row per agent, but the brain panel is shared with Agents. | Setup keeps the existing two-card chooser (OpenRouter or Local) inside the new panel. | Same behaviour on both pages, and one brain component to maintain. |
| P24 | Setup wording: the Ready step's main button, the plan buttons, and Back on steps that do not apply. | "Go to Home" until SP3 brings "Open a session". The plan buttons are named after the work ("Update coding agents", "Install coding agents"). Back skips steps that do not apply, just as Continue does. | Buttons say what they do. |
| P25 | Hermes and OpenClaw dashboards: the app does not know their addresses. | Agents links to each one's default address and says so ("its default address, it opens only while it is running"). | Honest, with no new API. A real check can come later. |
| P26 | Home's h1, Agents' safeguards and Safety's level words (the prototype's wording assumes sessions). | The h1 is the menu name ("Home"). Only safeguards true today are listed. The level words describe today's runs. Each page's draft decisions table lists the details (D-C2, D-D1, D-D2). | Copy must be true when shipped. Session wording arrives with SP3. |
| P27 | The shared brain-choice cards (`brain.css`, `BrainOpenRouterCard`, `BrainLocalCard`, `BrainModelActions`, `SetupBrainPanel`, used by Setup and Agents). | In SP2 they keep their behaviour and their SP1 look: they already use the Cobalt tokens. Setup (B4) and Agents (D1) place them inside the new layouts, and D1 only changes their heading level. A full restyle of these cards is a follow-up task after SP2. | Two pages share them, and restyling them inside either page task would spread one change across two reviews. |

## Order of work

The tasks depend on each other's files and fields, so run them in this order. Two tasks never edit the same file at the same time.

| # | Task | Needs first |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | C1 Page kit | none |
| 2 | A1 Team Room server: agreement asks first, pause, clock | none |
| 3 | A2 Team Room server: decisions resume the room, Continue | A1 |
| 4 | A4 Team Room Undo never throws away a later change | A1, A2 |
| 5 | B1 Setup safety: no `--yes`, no Hermes update step | none |
| 6 | B2 Workspace: who saved each file | A1 (the save records exist only after Approve) |
| 7 | C3 Runs page and the New run dialog | C1 |
| 8 | C2 Home page | C1, C3 (`runsBoard.ts`, `task.line`) |
| 9 | A3 Team Room page | C1, A1, A2, C3 (the shared run console and modal) |
| 10 | B3 Workspace page | C1, B2, A4 |
| 11 | B4 Setup page | C1, B1 |
| 12 | D1 Agents page | C1, C2, C3 |
| 13 | D2 Safety page | C1, C2, B1 |
| 14 | D3 SP1 leftovers and the SP2 sweeps | all of the above |
| 15 | E1 SP2 verification (orchestrator) | D3 |

`test/team-room.test.js` is edited by A1, then A2, then A4, in that order. No other task touches it.

### Task C1: Page kit (PageHeader, Banner, Tabs, Meter, EmptyState, StatusWord, table classes)

This task builds the one shared set of page pieces that every SP2 page task (A-D) consumes by name. It has no server work and no data calls: everything is props in, markup out. The Sessions placeholder page is its first consumer, so the kit is seen working in the real app before any big page needs it. **Every page task depends on this one; land C1 first.**

| Existing | Decision |

The prototype's status words use circle icons for nine states, `StatusMark` has five shapes. Both follow "shape plus words, never colour alone". `StatusMark` stays for the Home instrument bar and `Chip`. |
| `Chip.tsx`, `.os-chip` | Left alone. The kit only adds a pressed look for `button.os-chip` (Workspace's "Saved by agents" filter needs it). |
| `Panel.tsx`, `.os-panel` | Left alone. A `Banner` is a flat tinted strip, not a raised panel, so it does not wrap `Panel`. Page tasks keep using `.os-panel` for cards. |
| `Readout.tsx` | Left alone (large mono numbers). |
| `SegmentMeter.tsx` (class `.os-meter`, in `fleet.css`; `teamRoom.css` also styles `.os-team .os-meter`) | Left alone. It is a row of discrete segments for agents. The new continuous bar is `Meter.tsx` with its own class `.os-gauge`, so the two never collide. |

**What the worker must keep (the traps this kit already hit while being drafted):**
- **`.os-gauge`, never `.os-meter`.** See the table above.
- **Button colours.** `.os-shell button { color }` (specificity 0,1,1) beats a lone one-class rule, so the tab and chip rules are written `.os-tabs .os-tab` and `.os-shell button.os-chip`. Do not simplify them.
- **Old global `h1` rule** (`src/styles.css`: `clamp(32px, 5vw, 54px)`, line height 0.98, bottom margin 10px). The page title is written `.os-page-head .os-page-head__title` (two classes) so it wins.
- **Global `box-sizing: border-box`** comes from `src/agent-os.css` line 8. The kit relies on it (row heights are `min-height` with padding).
- **The calm Meter tone is soft ink, not cobalt.** The prototype draws the 38% bar in `--os-text-2`, and the Global Constraints keep cobalt for the primary action, the live state and the focus ring. The prop value is still called `"accent"` (the controller's fixed name); it is simply the default, calm tone.
- **Colour is never the only signal.** For the `warn` and `danger` Meter tones the page must put the reason in `detail` in words. A `Banner` always shows an icon shape and words.
- **No sideways scroll at 1024.** A flexible table column is always written `minmax(0, 1fr)`, never a bare `1fr`.

**Usage notes for the page tasks (what the other tasks may rely on):**
- Table markup (the page writes it; the roles keep it a table for screen readers):

```tsx
import type { CSSProperties } from "react";
const COLS = { "--os-table-cols": "160px minmax(0, 1fr) 120px 70px" } as CSSProperties;

<div className="os-table" role="table" aria-label="Runs" style={COLS}>
  <div className="os-table__head" role="row">
    <span className="os-table__cell" role="columnheader">State</span>
    <span className="os-table__cell" role="columnheader">Task</span>
    <span className="os-table__cell" role="columnheader">Agent</span>
    <span className="os-table__cell os-table__cell--end" role="columnheader">Time</span>
  </div>
  <div className="os-table__row" role="row">
    <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell"><StatusWord state="held" /></div>
    <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell">
      <span className="os-table__title os-trunc" title={fullTitle}>{fullTitle}</span>
      <span className="os-table__sub">Plan limit reached, resets 2:21 am</span>
    </div>
    <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell">Claude Code</div>
    <div className="os-table__cell os-table__cell--end os-mono" role="cell">20 s</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

- Tabs and their panel: `<Tabs label="Runs views" idPrefix="runs" tabs={[{ id: "board", label: "Board", count: 3 }, { id: "recordings", label: "Session recordings" }]} value={view} onChange={setView} />` then `<div {...tabPanelProps("runs", view)}>...</div>`. Rendering only the selected panel is fine; rendering all panels with `hidden` on the others also works.
- A finished run is `<StatusWord state="ready" label="Finished" />`; an unknown status is `<StatusWord state="unknown" />` (shows "—"); while a value loads use `<StatusWord state="loading" />` (shows "…").
- A banner with buttons: `<Banner tone="warn" title="Your Claude Code plan ran out." actions={<><button className="os-btn os-btn--ghost">Wait for reset</button><button className="os-btn os-btn--secondary">Keep going on OpenRouter</button></>}>Keep the same conversation going on OpenRouter, or wait for the reset.</Banner>`.
- A meter with an unknown value: `<Meter label="Spend today" value={null} detail="Unknown for subscription agents." />` (shows "—", draws no bar).
- A page's h1 text is the menu name (Home, Sessions, ...). Page title ids stay as today (for example `os-sessions-title`), and the `<section>` that wraps the page uses `aria-labelledby` with it.

**States and copy the kit itself shows (it has no data calls, so there is no loading or offline state of its own):**

| Piece | States | Exact words |
|---|---|---|
| PageHeader | with and without `eyebrow`, `lede`, `actions`; actions wrap under the title in a narrow window | Words come from the page. The Sessions page lede: "Work with your agents in their own real terminal, right here." |
| Banner | info, ok, warn, danger; with or without title and actions | From the page. |
| Tabs | selected, unselected, hover, focus; count shown (including 0); `value` that matches no tab leaves all unselected and the first tab reachable | From the page. |
| Meter | known value (calm, warn, danger); `null` or not a number shows "—" and says "unknown" to screen readers; values below 0 or above 1 are clamped | "—" for unknown. |
| EmptyState | with and without `body`, with and without `action`; wraps the button under the words in a narrow window | Sessions page: title "Sessions are coming", button "Open Runs". |
| StatusWord | the nine states with defaults Live, Ready, Waiting for you, Idle, Held, Failed, Stopped, "—" (spoken "Status unknown"), "…" (spoken "Loading"); `label` replaces the word | See the left column. |

**Sessions page copy (the only page the kit task changes):**
- The title and lede are unchanged: "Sessions", "Work with your agents in their own real terminal, right here."
- The empty state title is "Sessions are coming". Its body is the old first paragraph, then "Until then, your background runs are on Runs." The old text sent the person to Agents to start a run. SP2 removes that launch panel from Agents (runs start from Runs), so the new text points to Runs, and its button is "Open Runs" (`navigateTo("runs")`). It says "your background runs are on Runs" rather than "start a run from Runs", so it stays true before Task C3 lands the New run dialog.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing probe.** Create `.superpowers/ui-audit/probes/kit2.mjs` (git-ignored). There is no Storybook in this project, so the probe is the kit's test. It does two things. Part A checks the Sessions page, the first page built on the kit. Part B bundles the real kit components with esbuild into a small gallery and mounts it under the Sessions page, so each component is checked with the app's own CSS, fonts and tokens (Tabs keyboard, roving tabindex and `aria-selected` are checked there). Nothing in `src/` is touched by the probe.

```js
// C1: the shared page kit, mounted for real in the running app.
// Run from the worktree root, after `npm run build`:
//   node .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs probe .superpowers/ui-audit/probes/kit2.mjs
// Part A checks the Sessions page, the first page built on the kit. Part B bundles the
// real kit components with esbuild (already in node_modules, it is Vite's bundler) into
// a small gallery and mounts it under the page, so every component is checked with the
// app's own CSS, fonts and tokens. Nothing in src/ is touched.
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { mkdir } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";

const GALLERY_SOURCE = String.raw`
import { useState } from "react";
import type { CSSProperties } from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Boxes, Check } from "lucide-react";
import Banner from "./src/ui/components/Banner";
import EmptyState from "./src/ui/components/EmptyState";
import Meter from "./src/ui/components/Meter";
import PageHeader from "./src/ui/components/PageHeader";
import StatusWord from "./src/ui/components/StatusWord";
import type { StatusState } from "./src/ui/components/StatusWord";
import Tabs, { tabPanelProps } from "./src/ui/components/Tabs";

const TABS = [
  { id: "board", label: "Board", count: 3 },
  { id: "recordings", label: "Session recordings", count: 0 },
  { id: "third", label: "Third tab" }
];
const STATES: StatusState[] = ["live", "ready", "waiting", "idle", "held", "failed", "stopped", "unknown", "loading"];
const COLS = { "--os-table-cols": "160px minmax(0, 1fr) 120px 70px" } as CSSProperties;
const LONG = "Refactor the parser in a really quite long task title that goes on and on. ".repeat(6).trim();
const gap = (n: number): CSSProperties => ({ display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", gap: n });

function Gallery() {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState("board");
  const [pressed, setPressed] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div id="kit2-gallery" style={gap(32)}>
      <div id="kit2-head">
        <PageHeader
          eyebrow="Kit eyebrow"
          title="Gallery title"
          titleId="kit2-title"
          lede="A lede line in plain English."
          actions={<button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--primary">Main action</button>}
        />
      </div>
      <div id="kit2-banners" style={gap(12)}>
        <Banner tone="info">A plain notice.</Banner>
        <Banner tone="ok" title="Claude Code is up to date.">The ready tone.</Banner>
        <Banner
          tone="warn"
          title="Your Claude Code plan ran out."
          actions={<><button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--ghost">Wait for reset</button><button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--secondary">Keep going on OpenRouter</button></>}
        >
          Keep the same conversation going on OpenRouter (pay per use), or wait for the reset.
        </Banner>
        <Banner tone="danger" title="Codex CLI failed after 9 s.">The failure tone.</Banner>
      </div>
      <div id="kit2-tabs" style={gap(12)}>
        <Tabs label="Kit views" idPrefix="kit2" tabs={TABS} value={tab} onChange={setTab} />
        {TABS.map((t) => (
          <div key={t.id} {...tabPanelProps("kit2", t.id)} hidden={t.id !== tab}>Panel for {t.label}</div>
        ))}
        <div>
          <button type="button" id="kit2-chip" className="os-chip" aria-pressed={pressed} onClick={() => setPressed(!pressed)}>
            {pressed ? <Check size={14} aria-hidden="true" /> : null}Saved by agents
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="kit2-meters" style={{ ...gap(20), maxWidth: 420 }}>
        <Meter label="Context used" value={0.375} />
        <Meter label="Plan used (5-hour limit)" value={0.72} tone="warn" detail="Close to the limit. It resets at 2:21 am." />
        <Meter label="Plan used" value={1} tone="danger" detail="The limit is reached." />
        <Meter label="Spend today" value={null} detail="Unknown for subscription agents." />
        <Meter label="Over range" value={1.4} />
        <Meter label="Under range" value={-0.2} />
        <Meter label="Not a number" value={Number.NaN} />
      </div>
      <div id="kit2-status" style={{ display: "flex", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: "12px 24px" }}>
        {STATES.map((s) => <StatusWord key={s} state={s} />)}
        <StatusWord state="ready" label="Finished" />
      </div>
      <div id="kit2-empty">
        <EmptyState
          icon={Boxes}
          title="No runs in the air"
          body="A run appears here while an agent works on it, then moves to Landed."
          action={<button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--primary">New run</button>}
        />
      </div>
      <div id="kit2-table" className="os-table" role="table" aria-label="Sample runs" style={COLS}>
        <div className="os-table__head" role="row">
          <span className="os-table__cell" role="columnheader">State</span>
          <span className="os-table__cell" role="columnheader">Task</span>
          <span className="os-table__cell" role="columnheader">Agent</span>
          <span className="os-table__cell os-table__cell--end" role="columnheader">Time</span>
        </div>
        <div className="os-table__row" role="row">
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell"><StatusWord state="held" /></div>
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell"><span className="os-table__title">Add a settings page</span><span className="os-table__sub">Plan limit reached, resets 2:21 am</span></div>
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell">Claude Code</div>
          <div className="os-table__cell os-table__cell--end os-mono" role="cell">20 s</div>
        </div>
        <div className="os-table__row" role="row">
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell"><StatusWord state="failed" /></div>
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell"><span className="os-table__title os-trunc" title={LONG}>{LONG}</span></div>
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell">Codex CLI</div>
          <div className="os-table__cell os-table__cell--end os-mono" role="cell">9 s</div>
        </div>
        <div className="os-table__group">Landed <span>1 run</span></div>
        <div className="os-table__row" role="row">
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell"><StatusWord state="ready" label="Finished" /></div>
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell"><span className="os-table__title">Describe this project</span></div>
          <div className="os-table__cell" role="cell">Claude Code</div>
          <div className="os-table__cell os-table__cell--end os-mono" role="cell">42 s</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

const host = document.createElement("div");
host.id = "kit2-host";
(document.querySelector(".os-content") || document.body).appendChild(host);
createRoot(host).render(<Gallery />);
`;

const SIZES = [[1470, 956], [1280, 720], [1024, 640]];
const WORDS = { live: "Live", ready: "Ready", waiting: "Waiting for you", idle: "Idle", held: "Held", failed: "Failed", stopped: "Stopped", unknown: "—", loading: "…" };

export default async function ({ browser, openPage, pass, fail, HERE }) {
  const REPO = path.resolve(HERE, "..", "..");
  const colorOf = (tab, token) =>
    tab.evaluate((name) => {
      const probe = document.createElement("span");
      probe.style.color = `var(${name})`;
      document.body.appendChild(probe);
      const value = getComputedStyle(probe).color;
      probe.remove();
      return value;
    }, token);
  const shotElement = async (tab, selector, w, h, name) => {
    const dir = path.join(HERE, "shots", "kit2", `${w}x${h}`);
    await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    await tab.locator(selector).screenshot({ path: path.join(dir, `${name}.png`) });
  };

  // ---- Part A: the Sessions page is the first consumer ----
  for (const [w, h] of SIZES) {
    const { context, tab, errors } = await openPage(browser, w, h, "sessions");
    const page = await tab.evaluate(() => {
      const section = document.querySelector('section[aria-labelledby="os-sessions-title"]');
      const h1 = section?.querySelector("header.os-page-head h1#os-sessions-title");
      const empty = section?.querySelector(".os-empty");
      const style = h1 ? getComputedStyle(h1) : null;
      return {
        hasSection: Boolean(section),
        h1Count: document.querySelectorAll("h1").length,
        h1Text: h1?.textContent || "",
        fontSize: style?.fontSize || "",
        fontStretch: style?.fontStretch || "",
        letterSpacing: style?.letterSpacing || "",
        lede: section?.querySelector(".os-page-head__lede")?.textContent || "",
        emptyTitle: empty?.querySelector(".os-empty__title")?.textContent || "",
        emptyBorder: empty ? getComputedStyle(empty).borderTopStyle : "",
        buttons: [...(empty?.querySelectorAll("button") || [])].map((b) => b.textContent.trim()),
        legacy: document.querySelectorAll(".aos-phase-page, .os-sessions-soon").length,
        sideways: document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth > document.scrollingElement.clientWidth
      };
    });
    const want = w > 1440 ? "34px" : "32px";
    page.hasSection && page.h1Count === 1 && page.h1Text === "Sessions" ? pass(`sessions: one h1 "Sessions" in a PageHeader @${w}`) : fail(`sessions h1 @${w}`, JSON.stringify(page));
    page.fontSize === want && page.fontStretch === "87.5%" && parseFloat(page.letterSpacing) < 0 ? pass(`sessions: h1 is ${want}, condensed, tight @${w}`) : fail(`sessions h1 style @${w}`, `${page.fontSize} ${page.fontStretch} ${page.letterSpacing}`);
    page.lede === "Work with your agents in their own real terminal, right here." ? pass(`sessions: lede copy @${w}`) : fail(`sessions lede @${w}`, page.lede);
    page.emptyTitle === "Sessions are coming" && page.emptyBorder === "dashed" && page.buttons.join() === "Open Runs" ? pass(`sessions: EmptyState with "Open Runs" @${w}`) : fail(`sessions empty @${w}`, JSON.stringify(page));
    page.legacy === 0 ? pass(`sessions: no legacy aos-phase-page / os-sessions-soon @${w}`) : fail(`sessions legacy @${w}`, String(page.legacy));
    page.sideways ? fail(`sessions @${w}`, "sideways scroll") : pass(`sessions: no sideways scroll @${w}`);
    errors.length ? fail(`sessions console @${w}`, errors.join(" | ").slice(0, 300)) : pass(`sessions: console clean @${w}`);
    if (w === 1470) {
      try {
        await tab.getByRole("button", { name: "Open Runs" }).click({ timeout: 3000 });
        await tab.waitForTimeout(500);
        const now = await tab.evaluate(() => ({ page: new URL(location.href).searchParams.get("page"), current: document.querySelector('.os-nav__item[aria-current="page"]')?.textContent?.trim() || "" }));
        now.page === "runs" && /Runs/.test(now.current) ? pass("sessions: Open Runs goes to Runs") : fail("sessions: Open Runs", JSON.stringify(now));
      } catch {
        fail("sessions: Open Runs", "no Open Runs button to click");
      }
    }
    await context.close();
  }

  // ---- Part B: every kit component, mounted in the app ----
  let bundle = null;
  try {
    const { build } = createRequire(path.join(REPO, "package.json"))("esbuild");
    const result = await build({
      stdin: { contents: GALLERY_SOURCE, resolveDir: REPO, loader: "tsx", sourcefile: "kit2-gallery.tsx" },
      bundle: true, write: false, format: "iife", platform: "browser", jsx: "automatic", logLevel: "silent",
      define: { "process.env.NODE_ENV": '"production"' }
    });
    bundle = result.outputFiles[0].text;
    pass("gallery bundle builds from the real kit components");
  } catch (error) {
    fail("gallery bundle", String(error.errors?.[0]?.text || error.message).slice(0, 200));
  }
  if (!bundle) return;

  for (const [w, h] of SIZES) {
    const { context, tab, errors } = await openPage(browser, w, h, "sessions");
    await tab.evaluate(bundle);
    await tab.waitForSelector("#kit2-gallery", { timeout: 5000 });
    await tab.waitForTimeout(300);

    // Layout, at every size.
    const layout = await tab.evaluate(() => {
      const table = document.querySelector("#kit2-table");
      const lefts = (row, selector) => [...row.querySelectorAll(selector)].map((c) => Math.round(c.getBoundingClientRect().left));
      const rows = [...table.querySelectorAll(".os-table__row")];
      const head = lefts(table.querySelector(".os-table__head"), ":scope > .os-table__cell");
      const trunc = table.querySelector(".os-trunc");
      const banners = [...document.querySelectorAll("#kit2-banners .os-banner")];
      const box = document.querySelector("#kit2-banners").getBoundingClientRect();
      return {
        aligned: rows.every((row) => lefts(row, ":scope > .os-table__cell").every((x, i) => Math.abs(x - head[i]) <= 1)),
        rowHeights: rows.map((r) => Math.round(r.getBoundingClientRect().height)),
        rowTops: rows.map((r) => getComputedStyle(r).borderTopWidth),
        headBorder: getComputedStyle(table.querySelector(".os-table__head")).borderBottomWidth,
        ellipsis: trunc.scrollWidth > trunc.clientWidth && getComputedStyle(trunc).textOverflow === "ellipsis",
        endAlign: getComputedStyle(table.querySelector(".os-table__cell--end")).textAlign,
        tableInside: table.getBoundingClientRect().right <= document.documentElement.clientWidth + 0.5,
        bannersInside: banners.every((b) => b.getBoundingClientRect().right <= box.right + 0.5),
        sideways: document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth > document.scrollingElement.clientWidth
      };
    });
    layout.aligned ? pass(`table: head and row columns line up @${w}`) : fail(`table columns @${w}`, "cell lefts differ");
    layout.rowHeights.every((x) => x >= 52) ? pass(`table: rows are at least 52px @${w}`) : fail(`table rows @${w}`, layout.rowHeights.join());
    layout.rowTops.join() === "0px,1px,0px" && layout.headBorder === "1px" ? pass(`table: hairlines (none under head or group, one between rows) @${w}`) : fail(`table hairlines @${w}`, `${layout.rowTops.join()} head=${layout.headBorder}`);
    layout.ellipsis ? pass(`table: a long title ends in an ellipsis @${w}`) : fail(`table ellipsis @${w}`, "not truncated");
    layout.endAlign === "right" && layout.tableInside ? pass(`table: end cell right-aligned, table inside the window @${w}`) : fail(`table end cell @${w}`, JSON.stringify(layout));
    layout.bannersInside ? pass(`banners stay inside their column @${w}`) : fail(`banners overflow @${w}`, "a banner is wider than its column");
    layout.sideways ? fail(`gallery @${w}`, "sideways scroll") : pass(`gallery: no sideways scroll @${w}`);
    await shotElement(tab, "#kit2-gallery", w, h, "gallery");

    if (w === 1470) {
      // PageHeader
      const head = await tab.evaluate(() => {
        const header = document.querySelector("#kit2-head header.os-page-head");
        const h1 = header?.querySelector("h1#kit2-title");
        const actions = header?.querySelector(".os-page-head__actions");
        return {
          tag: header?.tagName, h1: h1?.textContent, eyebrow: header?.querySelector(".os-page-head__eyebrow.os-micro")?.textContent,
          lede: header?.querySelector(".os-page-head__lede")?.textContent, action: actions?.textContent,
          sameRow: actions && h1 ? actions.getBoundingClientRect().top < h1.getBoundingClientRect().bottom : false,
          flushRight: actions && header ? Math.abs(actions.getBoundingClientRect().right - header.getBoundingClientRect().right) <= 1 : false
        };
      });
      head.tag === "HEADER" && head.h1 === "Gallery title" && head.eyebrow === "Kit eyebrow" && head.lede === "A lede line in plain English." && head.action === "Main action" ? pass("PageHeader: eyebrow, h1 with titleId, lede and actions") : fail("PageHeader", JSON.stringify(head));
      head.sameRow && head.flushRight ? pass("PageHeader: actions sit on the title row, flush right") : fail("PageHeader layout", JSON.stringify(head));

      // Banner
      const banners = await tab.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll("#kit2-banners .os-banner")].map((b) => {
        const style = getComputedStyle(b);
        return {
          tone: b.className.replace("os-banner os-banner--", ""), role: b.getAttribute("role"), title: b.querySelector(".os-banner__title")?.textContent || "",
          iconHidden: b.querySelector("svg.os-banner__icon")?.getAttribute("aria-hidden"),
          widths: [style.borderTopWidth, style.borderLeftWidth, style.borderRightWidth, style.borderBottomWidth].join(),
          buttons: b.querySelectorAll(".os-banner__actions button").length,
          iconColor: getComputedStyle(b.querySelector("svg.os-banner__icon")).color,
          plain: Boolean(b.querySelector(".os-banner__body--plain"))
        };
      }));
      const roles = banners.map((b) => `${b.tone}:${b.role}`).join();
      roles === "info:status,ok:status,warn:alert,danger:alert" ? pass("Banner: info and ok are status, warn and danger are alert") : fail("Banner roles", roles);
      banners.every((b) => b.widths === "1px,1px,1px,1px" && b.iconHidden === "true") ? pass("Banner: 1px border on every side (no thick left border), icon hidden from screen readers") : fail("Banner chrome", JSON.stringify(banners));
      banners[0].plain && !banners[0].title && banners[1].title === "Claude Code is up to date." && banners[2].buttons === 2 ? pass("Banner: plain body, title, and actions render") : fail("Banner content", JSON.stringify(banners));
      const want = { info: "--os-accent-strong", ok: "--os-ok", warn: "--os-warn", danger: "--os-danger" };
      for (const b of banners) {
        const token = await colorOf(tab, want[b.tone]);
        b.iconColor === token ? pass(`Banner: ${b.tone} icon uses ${want[b.tone]}`) : fail(`Banner ${b.tone} colour`, `${b.iconColor} vs ${token}`);
      }

      // Tabs: roles, roving tabindex, arrows, Home, End, click
      const read = () => tab.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll("#kit2-tabs [role=tab]")].map((t) => ({
        id: t.id, selected: t.getAttribute("aria-selected"), tabindex: t.getAttribute("tabindex"), controls: t.getAttribute("aria-controls"), focused: document.activeElement === t
      })));
      const summary = (s) => s.map((t) => `${t.selected === "true" ? "S" : "o"}${t.tabindex}${t.focused ? "F" : "_"}`).join(" ");
      const panels = () => tab.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll("#kit2-tabs [role=tabpanel]")].map((p) => ({ id: p.id, labelled: p.getAttribute("aria-labelledby"), hidden: p.hidden })));
      let s = await read();
      const wiring = s.every((t) => t.controls === t.id.replace("-tab-", "-panel-")) && s.map((t) => t.id).join() === "kit2-tab-board,kit2-tab-recordings,kit2-tab-third";
      const p0 = await panels();
      wiring && p0.every((p) => p.labelled === p.id.replace("-panel-", "-tab-")) && p0.filter((p) => !p.hidden).map((p) => p.id).join() === "kit2-panel-board" ? pass("Tabs: ids, aria-controls and the panel's aria-labelledby line up") : fail("Tabs wiring", JSON.stringify({ s, p0 }));
      summary(s) === "S0_ o-1_ o-1_" ? pass("Tabs: first tab selected, the only tab stop (tabindex 0)") : fail("Tabs initial", summary(s));
      const counts = await tab.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll("#kit2-tabs .os-tab__count")].map((c) => ({ text: c.textContent, mono: /JetBrains Mono/.test(getComputedStyle(c).fontFamily) })));
      counts.length === 2 && counts[0].text === "3" && counts[1].text === "0" && counts.every((c) => c.mono) ? pass("Tabs: counts shown in mono (0 shows 0, no count shows nothing)") : fail("Tabs counts", JSON.stringify(counts));
      await tab.locator("#kit2-tab-board").focus();
      const press = async (key, expected, name) => {
        await tab.keyboard.press(key);
        const now = await read();
        summary(now) === expected ? pass(`Tabs: ${name}`) : fail(`Tabs ${name}`, `${summary(now)} (wanted ${expected})`);
      };
      await press("ArrowRight", "o-1_ S0F o-1_", "ArrowRight selects and focuses the next tab");
      await press("ArrowRight", "o-1_ o-1_ S0F", "ArrowRight again reaches the last tab");
      await press("ArrowRight", "S0F o-1_ o-1_", "ArrowRight wraps from last to first");
      await press("ArrowLeft", "o-1_ o-1_ S0F", "ArrowLeft wraps from first to last");
      await press("Home", "S0F o-1_ o-1_", "Home goes to the first tab");
      await press("End", "o-1_ o-1_ S0F", "End goes to the last tab");
      await press("Alt+ArrowLeft", "o-1_ o-1_ S0F", "Alt+Arrow is left to the browser");
      const p1 = await panels();
      p1.filter((p) => !p.hidden).map((p) => p.id).join() === "kit2-panel-third" ? pass("Tabs: the page's panel follows the selection") : fail("Tabs panel", JSON.stringify(p1));
      const ring = await tab.evaluate(() => { const c = getComputedStyle(document.activeElement); return `${c.outlineStyle} ${c.outlineWidth}`; });
      ring === "solid 2px" ? pass("Tabs: the focused tab shows the 2px focus ring") : fail("Tabs focus ring", ring);
      await tab.keyboard.press("Tab");
      const afterTab = await tab.evaluate(() => ({ role: document.activeElement.getAttribute("role"), id: document.activeElement.id }));
      afterTab.role !== "tab" && afterTab.id === "kit2-chip" ? pass("Tabs: the Tab key leaves the tab row") : fail("Tabs Tab key", JSON.stringify(afterTab));
      await tab.keyboard.press("Shift+Tab");
      s = await read();
      summary(s) === "o-1_ o-1_ S0F" ? pass("Tabs: Shift+Tab comes back to the selected tab") : fail("Tabs Shift+Tab", summary(s));
      await tab.locator("#kit2-tab-recordings").click();
      s = await read();
      summary(s) === "o-1_ S0F o-1_" ? pass("Tabs: a click selects and focuses") : fail("Tabs click", summary(s));
      await tab.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: "reduce" });
      const motion = await tab.evaluate(() => parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.querySelector("#kit2-tabs .os-tab")).transitionDuration));
      motion <= 0.001 ? pass("Tabs: transitions are off under reduced motion") : fail("Tabs reduced motion", String(motion));
      await tab.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: null });

      // Pressable chip
      const chipBefore = await tab.evaluate(() => ({ pressed: document.querySelector("#kit2-chip").getAttribute("aria-pressed"), bg: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector("#kit2-chip")).backgroundColor, svg: document.querySelectorAll("#kit2-chip svg").length }));
      await tab.locator("#kit2-chip").click();
      await tab.mouse.move(5, 5);
      await tab.waitForTimeout(300);
      const chipAfter = await tab.evaluate(() => ({ pressed: document.querySelector("#kit2-chip").getAttribute("aria-pressed"), bg: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector("#kit2-chip")).backgroundColor, svg: document.querySelectorAll("#kit2-chip svg").length }));
      chipBefore.pressed === "false" && chipAfter.pressed === "true" && chipBefore.bg !== chipAfter.bg && chipBefore.svg === 0 && chipAfter.svg === 1 ? pass("Chip: aria-pressed toggles, the fill changes, a check appears") : fail("Chip", JSON.stringify({ chipBefore, chipAfter }));

      meters[0].role === "meter" && meters[0].now === "38" && meters[0].min === "0" && meters[0].max === "100" && meters[0].labelledby ? pass("Meter: role=meter with value 38 of 0 to 100, named by its label") : fail("Meter aria", JSON.stringify(meters[0]));
      meters[3].role === null && meters[3].hidden === "true" && meters[3].ratio === 0 && /unknown/.test(await tab.locator("#kit2-meters .os-gauge").nth(3).textContent()) ? pass("Meter: null has no meter role, an empty bar and a spoken \"unknown\"") : fail("Meter null", JSON.stringify(meters[3]));
      meters[1].described === "Close to the limit. It resets at 2:21 am." && meters[2].ratio === 1 && meters[0].ratio === 0.38 && meters.every((m) => m.height === 6) ? pass("Meter: detail is the description, the fill is the right length, the bar is 6px") : fail("Meter geometry", JSON.stringify(meters));
      const [soft, accent, warn, danger] = [await colorOf(tab, "--os-text-2"), await colorOf(tab, "--os-accent"), await colorOf(tab, "--os-warn"), await colorOf(tab, "--os-danger")];
      meters[0].fillColor === soft && meters[0].fillColor !== accent && meters[1].fillColor === warn && meters[2].fillColor === danger ? pass("Meter: calm tone is soft ink (not cobalt), warn and danger use their tokens") : fail("Meter colours", JSON.stringify(meters.map((m) => m.fillColor)));

      })));

      got === Object.entries(WORDS).map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`).join() ? pass("StatusWord: the nine default words") : fail("StatusWord words", got);

      const tokens = { ready: "--os-ok", live: "--os-accent-strong", waiting: "--os-warn", idle: "--os-text-3", held: "--os-warn", failed: "--os-danger", stopped: "--os-warn" };
      for (const [state, token] of Object.entries(tokens)) {

      }

      const empty = await tab.evaluate(() => {
        const e = document.querySelector("#kit2-empty .os-empty");
        return { svgHidden: e.querySelector("svg")?.getAttribute("aria-hidden"), title: e.querySelector(".os-empty__title")?.textContent, body: e.querySelector(".os-empty__body")?.textContent, action: e.querySelector(".os-empty__action button")?.textContent, border: getComputedStyle(e).borderTopStyle, height: e.getBoundingClientRect().height, heading: e.querySelectorAll("h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6").length };

    }
    errors.length ? fail(`gallery console @${w}`, errors.join(" | ").slice(0, 300)) : pass(`gallery: console clean @${w}`);
    await context.close();
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `src/ui/components/Banner.tsx`.** The icon comes from the tone (the same four icons as `Toast.tsx`), so the tone is never colour alone. Info and ok are polite (`role="status"`); warn and danger are `role="alert"`.

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { CheckCircle2, CircleAlert, Info, XCircle } from "lucide-react";

// A notice with an icon, a short title, some words and, if needed, buttons.
// The tone picks the icon and the wash. The tone is never the only signal:
// the icon shape and the words say it too. Info and ok are polite messages
// (role="status"); warn and danger interrupt (role="alert").
export type BannerTone = "info" | "ok" | "warn" | "danger";

const ICONS = { info: Info, ok: CheckCircle2, warn: CircleAlert, danger: XCircle } as const;

export interface BannerProps {
  tone: BannerTone;
  title?: ReactNode;
  children?: ReactNode;
  actions?: ReactNode;
}

export default function Banner({ tone, title, children, actions }: BannerProps) {
  const Icon = ICONS[tone];
  const role = tone === "warn" || tone === "danger" ? "alert" : "status";
  return (
    <div className={`os-banner os-banner--${tone}`} role={role}>
      <Icon className="os-banner__icon" size={20} aria-hidden="true" />
      <div className="os-banner__text">
        {title ? <p className="os-banner__title">{title}</p> : null}
        {children ? <div className={`os-banner__body${title ? "" : " os-banner__body--plain"}`}>{children}</div> : null}
      </div>
      {actions ? <div className="os-banner__actions">{actions}</div> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create `src/ui/components/Tabs.tsx`.** The WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with automatic activation. Only the selected tab is a Tab-key stop (roving `tabIndex`); Arrow Left/Right wrap round, Home and End jump; Alt, Ctrl and Cmd with an arrow are left to the browser. `onChange` is called first, then focus moves to the new tab, which already exists in the DOM (a button with `tabIndex -1` can be focused by code).

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import type { KeyboardEvent } from "react";

// A row of tabs that switch a panel (WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, automatic
// activation). Arrow Left/Right move and select (wrapping round), Home and End
// jump to the first and last. Only the selected tab is a Tab-key stop; the Tab
// key then goes on into the panel. The page renders the panel itself:
//   <div {...tabPanelProps("runs", value)}>...</div>
// which gives it role="tabpanel", the id this tab points at with aria-controls,
// and aria-labelledby back to the tab.
export interface TabItem {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  count?: number;
}

export interface TabsProps {
  label: string;
  idPrefix: string;
  tabs: TabItem[];
  value: string;
  onChange: (id: string) => void;
}

export const tabDomId = (idPrefix: string, id: string) => `${idPrefix}-tab-${id}`;
export const panelDomId = (idPrefix: string, id: string) => `${idPrefix}-panel-${id}`;

export function tabPanelProps(idPrefix: string, id: string) {
  return { role: "tabpanel" as const, id: panelDomId(idPrefix, id), "aria-labelledby": tabDomId(idPrefix, id) };
}

export default function Tabs({ label, idPrefix, tabs, value, onChange }: TabsProps) {
  const list = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const hasValue = tabs.some((tab) => tab.id === value);
  // If `value` matches no tab, the first tab is still reachable with the Tab key.
  const tabStop = hasValue ? value : tabs[0]?.id;

  function select(index: number) {
    if (tabs.length === 0) return;
    const next = (index + tabs.length) % tabs.length;
    onChange(tabs[next].id);
    list.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>('[role="tab"]')[next]?.focus();
  }

  function onKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLButtonElement>, index: number) {
    // Leave Alt/Ctrl/Cmd + arrow to the browser (history, text jumps).
    if (event.altKey || event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey) return;
    if (event.key === "ArrowRight") select(index + 1);
    else if (event.key === "ArrowLeft") select(index - 1);
    else if (event.key === "Home") select(0);
    else if (event.key === "End") select(tabs.length - 1);
    else return;
    event.preventDefault();
  }

  return (
    <div ref={list} className="os-tabs" role="tablist" aria-label={label}>
      {tabs.map((tab, index) => (
        <button
          key={tab.id}
          type="button"
          role="tab"
          id={tabDomId(idPrefix, tab.id)}
          className="os-tab"
          aria-selected={hasValue && tab.id === value}
          aria-controls={panelDomId(idPrefix, tab.id)}
          tabIndex={tab.id === tabStop ? 0 : -1}
          onClick={() => onChange(tab.id)}
          onKeyDown={(event) => onKeyDown(event, index)}
        >
          {tab.label}
          {typeof tab.count === "number" ? <span className="os-tab__count os-mono">{tab.count}</span> : null}
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create `src/ui/components/Meter.tsx`.** Value `0..1`. `null` or a non-finite number is the honest "—" (no bar, "unknown" for screen readers). When the value is known the bar is a real `role="meter"` named by its label and described by `detail`.

```tsx
import { useId } from "react";

// One continuous gauge, 0 to 1 (context used, plan used). `null` is an honest
// "—": the value is not known, so no bar is drawn. Not to be confused with
// SegmentMeter (one segment per agent, class .os-meter): this one is .os-gauge.
// For the warn and danger tones, put the reason in `detail` in words, because
// the colour alone must not carry the meaning.
export interface MeterProps {
  label: string;
  value: number | null;
  detail?: string;
  tone?: "accent" | "warn" | "danger";
}

export default function Meter({ label, value, detail, tone = "accent" }: MeterProps) {
  const labelId = useId();
  const detailId = useId();
  const ratio = typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value) ? Math.min(1, Math.max(0, value)) : null;
  const percent = ratio === null ? null : Math.round(ratio * 100);
  return (
    <div className={`os-gauge os-gauge--${tone}`}>
      <div className="os-gauge__top">
        <span id={labelId} className="os-gauge__label">
          {label}
        </span>
        <span className="os-gauge__value os-mono">
          {percent === null ? (
            <>
              <span aria-hidden="true">—</span>
              <span className="os-visually-hidden">unknown</span>
            </>
          ) : (
            `${percent}%`
          )}
        </span>
      </div>
      <div
        className="os-gauge__track"
        role={percent === null ? undefined : "meter"}
        aria-hidden={percent === null ? true : undefined}
        aria-labelledby={percent === null ? undefined : labelId}
        aria-describedby={percent !== null && detail ? detailId : undefined}
        aria-valuemin={percent === null ? undefined : 0}
        aria-valuemax={percent === null ? undefined : 100}
        aria-valuenow={percent ?? undefined}
      >
        <span className="os-gauge__fill" style={{ width: `${percent ?? 0}%` }} />
      </div>
      {detail ? (
        <p id={detailId} className="os-gauge__detail">
          {detail}
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// A designed "nothing here yet": a dashed outline, an icon, a title, a line of

  title: string;

}

      <Icon className="os-empty__icon" size={22} aria-hidden="true" />
      <div className="os-empty__text">

        {body ? <div className="os-empty__body">{body}</div> : null}
      </div>
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Create `src/ui/components/StatusWord.tsx`.** The nine-state vocabulary from the prototype (`AOS.statuses`), icon plus word. The colour is on the icon only. "unknown" and "loading" have no icon, because their words are "—" and "…".

```tsx
import { Activity, CircleCheck, CircleDashed, CircleHelp, CirclePause, CircleStop, CircleX } from "lucide-react";
import type { LucideIcon } from "lucide-react";

// One status vocabulary for every page: an icon and a word, colour only on the
// icon (never colour alone). `label` replaces the word, for example
// <StatusWord state="ready" label="Finished" />. "unknown" shows "—" and
// "loading" shows "…" (no icon); screen readers hear "Status unknown" and
// "Loading".
export type StatusState = "live" | "ready" | "waiting" | "idle" | "held" | "failed" | "stopped" | "unknown" | "loading";

const STATUS: Record<StatusState, { icon: LucideIcon | null; word: string; spoken?: string }> = {
  live: { icon: Activity, word: "Live" },
  ready: { icon: CircleCheck, word: "Ready" },
  waiting: { icon: CircleHelp, word: "Waiting for you" },
  idle: { icon: CircleDashed, word: "Idle" },
  held: { icon: CirclePause, word: "Held" },
  failed: { icon: CircleX, word: "Failed" },
  stopped: { icon: CircleStop, word: "Stopped" },
  unknown: { icon: null, word: "—", spoken: "Status unknown" },
  loading: { icon: null, word: "…", spoken: "Loading" }
};

export interface StatusWordProps {
  state: StatusState;
  label?: string;
}

export default function StatusWord({ state, label }: StatusWordProps) {
  const { icon: Icon, word, spoken } = STATUS[state];
  const custom = typeof label === "string" && label.trim() !== "";
  return (
    <span className={`os-statusword os-statusword--${state}`}>
      {Icon ? <Icon size={16} aria-hidden="true" /> : null}
      {Icon || custom ? (
        <span>{custom ? label : word}</span>
      ) : (
        <>
          <span aria-hidden="true">{word}</span>
          <span className="os-visually-hidden">{spoken}</span>
        </>
      )}
    </span>
  );
}
```

Values come from sections 7 to 11 of the prototype's `shared/cobalt.css` and `kit.html`, expressed in the `--os-*` tokens. /* Page kit (SP2): the pieces every core page shares. Tokens only (see

```css
   transitions off under prefers-reduced-motion.

/* ---- Page header (PageHeader.tsx) ------------------------------------- */
.os-page-head {

  transition: background var(--os-dur-quick) var(--os-ease-out), color var(--os-dur-quick) var(--os-ease-out), border-color var(--os-dur-quick) var(--os-ease-out);
}
.os-tabs .os-tab[aria-selected="true"] {
  background: var(--os-surface-3);
  border-color: var(--os-line-2);
  color: var(--os-text-1);
  box-shadow: var(--os-e1);
}
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
  .os-tabs .os-tab[aria-selected="false"]:hover {
    background: var(--os-surface-2);
    color: var(--os-text-1);
  }
}
.os-shell .os-tabs .os-tab:focus-visible {
  outline-offset: 1px;
}
.os-tab__count {
  font-size: var(--os-fs-12);
  color: var(--os-text-3);
}
/* surface-3 is too light for the faint ink (4.2:1), so the selected count is soft ink. */
.os-tabs .os-tab[aria-selected="true"] .os-tab__count {
  color: var(--os-text-2);
}

/* ---- Meter (Meter.tsx) ------------------------------------------------ */
/* .os-gauge, not .os-meter: .os-meter is the Home segment meter (fleet.css). */
.os-gauge {
  display: block;
  min-width: 0;
}
.os-gauge__top {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--os-sp-3);
  font-size: var(--os-fs-13);
  color: var(--os-text-2);
}
.os-gauge__value {
  font-size: var(--os-fs-13);
  color: var(--os-text-1);
}
.os-gauge__track {
  height: 6px;
  margin-top: var(--os-sp-2);
  border-radius: 3px;
  background: var(--os-line-2);
  overflow: hidden;
}
/* The calm tone is soft ink, as in the prototype: cobalt stays for the primary
   action, the live state and the focus ring. */
.os-gauge__fill {
  display: block;
  height: 100%;
  border-radius: inherit;
  background: var(--os-text-2);
  transition: width var(--os-dur-base) var(--os-ease-out);
}
.os-gauge--warn .os-gauge__fill {
  background: var(--os-warn);
}
.os-gauge--danger .os-gauge__fill {
  background: var(--os-danger);
}
.os-gauge__detail {
  margin: 5px 0 0;
  font-size: var(--os-fs-12);
  line-height: 1.4;
  color: var(--os-text-3);
}

/* ---- Empty state (EmptyState.tsx) ------------------------------------- */
.os-empty {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--os-sp-4);
  min-height: 80px;
  padding: var(--os-sp-3) var(--os-sp-4) var(--os-sp-3) var(--os-sp-5);
  border: 1px dashed var(--os-line-2);
  border-radius: var(--os-r-sm);
}
.os-empty__icon {
  flex: none;
  color: var(--os-text-3);
}
.os-empty__text {
  flex: 1 1 0;
  min-width: 0;
}
.os-empty__title {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: var(--os-fs-15);
  font-weight: 600;
  font-stretch: 90%;
  color: var(--os-text-1);
}
.os-empty__body {
  max-width: 70ch;
  margin: 2px 0 0;
  font-size: var(--os-fs-13);
  line-height: 1.45;
  color: var(--os-text-2);
}
.os-empty__action {
  flex: none;
}
@media (max-width: 720px) {
  .os-empty {
    flex-wrap: wrap;
  }
  .os-empty__action {
    flex-basis: 100%;
  }
}

/* ---- Status word (StatusWord.tsx) ------------------------------------- */
/* The colour is on the icon only. The word is always in full ink. */
.os-statusword {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--os-sp-2);
  color: var(--os-text-1);
  font-weight: 520;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.os-statusword svg {
  flex: none;
}
.os-statusword--ready svg {
  color: var(--os-ok);
}
.os-statusword--live svg {
  color: var(--os-accent-strong);
}
.os-statusword--waiting svg,
.os-statusword--held svg,
.os-statusword--stopped svg {
  color: var(--os-warn);
}
.os-statusword--failed svg {
  color: var(--os-danger);
}
.os-statusword--idle svg {
  color: var(--os-text-3);
}
.os-statusword--unknown,
.os-statusword--loading {
  color: var(--os-text-3);
  font-weight: 450;
}

/* ---- Tables: grid rows, hairlines, no boxes --------------------------- */
/* Markup (the page writes it; roles keep it a table for screen readers):
     <div class="os-table" role="table" aria-label="Runs"
          style="--os-table-cols: 134px minmax(0, 1fr) 138px 120px">
       <div class="os-table__head" role="row">
         <span class="os-table__cell" role="columnheader">Agent</span> ...
       </div>
       <div class="os-table__row" role="row">
         <div class="os-table__cell" role="cell">...</div> ...
       </div>
     </div>
   Always write a flexible column as `minmax(0, 1fr)`, never a bare `1fr`, or a
   long name pushes the page sideways. In React the page sets the variable in
   `style={{ "--os-table-cols": "..." } as React.CSSProperties}`. */
.os-table {
  width: 100%;
  min-width: 0;
}
.os-table__head,
.os-table__row {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: var(--os-table-cols, minmax(0, 1fr));
  column-gap: var(--os-table-gap, var(--os-sp-4));
  align-items: center;
}
.os-table__head {
  min-height: 32px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--os-line-1);
  font-size: var(--os-fs-12);
  font-weight: 560;
  letter-spacing: 0.01em;
  color: var(--os-text-3);
}
.os-table__row {
  min-height: 52px;
  padding: var(--os-sp-2) 0;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--os-line-1);
}
.os-table__head + .os-table__row,
.os-table__group + .os-table__row {
  border-top: 0;
}
.os-table__cell {
  min-width: 0;
}
.os-table__cell--end {
  text-align: right;
}
/* A row that is itself a link or button. */
a.os-table__row,
button.os-table__row {
  color: inherit;
  text-decoration: none;
  transition: background var(--os-dur-quick) var(--os-ease-out);
}
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
  a.os-table__row:hover,
  button.os-table__row:hover {
    background: var(--os-surface-1);
  }
}
.os-shell a.os-table__row:focus-visible,
.os-shell button.os-table__row:focus-visible {
  outline-offset: -2px;
}
/* A section label inside a table ("Operators 2"). */
.os-table__group {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: var(--os-sp-3);
  min-height: 40px;
  padding-top: var(--os-sp-4);
  font-size: var(--os-fs-13);
  font-weight: 620;
  font-stretch: 90%;
  color: var(--os-text-2);
}
.os-table__group > span {
  font-size: var(--os-fs-12);
  font-weight: 450;
  font-stretch: 100%;
  color: var(--os-text-3);
}
/* Two-line cell: a title, then a quiet line under it. */
.os-table__title {
  display: block;
  font-size: var(--os-fs-15);
  font-weight: 560;
  line-height: 1.3;
  color: var(--os-text-1);
}
.os-table__sub {
  display: block;
  margin-top: 2px;
  font-size: var(--os-fs-12);
  line-height: 1.35;
  color: var(--os-text-2);
}
/* One line that ends in "…". The page also sets title="" with the full text. */
.os-trunc {
  display: block;
  min-width: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  white-space: nowrap;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

/* ---- Pressable chip (a filter that is on or off) ---------------------- */
/* <button type="button" class="os-chip" aria-pressed={on}>, with a Check icon
   (size 14) in front while it is on. Wider than a label chip: 32 px tall. */
.os-shell button.os-chip {
  height: 32px;
  color: var(--os-text-2);
  font-weight: 540;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background var(--os-dur-quick) var(--os-ease-out), border-color var(--os-dur-quick) var(--os-ease-out), color var(--os-dur-quick) var(--os-ease-out);
}
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
  .os-shell button.os-chip:hover {
    border-color: var(--os-line-3);
    color: var(--os-text-1);
  }
}
.os-shell button.os-chip[aria-pressed="true"] {
  background: var(--os-surface-3);
  border-color: var(--os-text-2);
  color: var(--os-text-1);
}
.os-shell button.os-chip:disabled {
  color: var(--os-disabled);
  border-color: var(--os-line-1);
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Task A1: Team Room server: agreement asks first, the room pauses, the clock stops

Spec: D10 and "Team Room server change (D10)" items 1, 2, 3 and 6. After this task, two agents agreeing on a file saves nothing: the room stops at the end of that turn as `needs_you`, with a new field `pausedFor` naming the proposal, and its time limit stops running. The early "agreed, file saved" exit is gone, and a room ends `agreed` only at its turn or time limit with an approved file saved and nothing still open. (Approve/Reject resuming the room, and Continue accepting a paused room, are Task A2; the one-line `continueRoom` reset below is only here so the rewritten undo test can Continue past a pause.)

**Files:**
- Modify: `server/runtime/team-room/moderator.js` (header comment lines 8-11; import line 20; `finish` lines 248-257 plus a new `pauseRoom`; `resolveAgreement` lines 274-297; `applyReply` start 300-302 and its `agree` branch line 360; `limitReached` lines 398-420; `runRoom` limit call (line 548), the timed-out branch (lines 572-576) and the early-exit block (lines 587-595); `continueRoom` meta update (lines 651-657))
- Modify: `server/runtime/team-room/room-store.js` (`createRoom` meta lines 113-140; `summarizeRoom` lines 187-210)
- Modify: `server/runtime/team-room/protocol.js` (the two sentences in `buildTurnPromptDetailed`, lines 257 and 268)
- Modify: `server/runtime/team-room/actions.js` (two comments only, lines 3-4 and 89-91)
- Test: `test/team-room.test.js` (imports lines 21 and 34-43; new section "4b" inserted before the "5. The HTTP router" banner at line 1235; ten existing tests rewritten, listed in Step 4)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (existing, unchanged):
  - `applyFileProposal(roomId, proposalId)` from `server/runtime/team-room/actions.js`. Returns the action record; throws `roomError(403, "execution_gate_off", ...)` with the gate off. The tests below call it directly as "Approve". `moderator.js` stops importing it.
  - `createModerator({ runManager, now, minTurnTimeoutMs, turnGraceMs })`, `recoverStaleRooms()`, `setExecutionGateStatus`, and the test helpers at the top of the test file (`setScript`, `withTeamEnv`, `runRoom`, `fileReply`, `teamFile`, `exists`, `promptsOf`, `withRouter`, `subscribeRoom`).
- Produces:
  - `meta.json` gains `pausedFor: string | null` (the proposal id, for example `"P1"`) and `clockUsedMs: number | null` (milliseconds of the room's clock used when it paused). `createRoom` writes both as `null`. They are set together when the room pauses and cleared (`null`) by every other ending and by `continueRoom`.
  - `summarizeRoom(meta, decision)` (the list rows of `GET /api/team-rooms`) gains `pausedFor: string | null`.
  - The pause is the existing status `needs_you`, plus `pausedFor`. Its `endReason` and the final `status` event's `reason` are exactly: `Paused for your decision: <proposer label>'s file <name> needs your approval.` (for example `Paused for your decision: Hermes Agent's file plan.md needs your approval.`). The `status` event also carries `pausedFor`.
  - Agreement copy on the proposal (`statusReason`), gate on or off: `Both agents agree. Waiting for your approval.`
  - End reasons (exact): turn limit with an approved, saved file and nothing open or waiting: status `agreed`, `Reached the limit of <n> turns with your approved file saved and nothing left open.`; time limit: `Reached the <m>-minute time limit with your approved file saved and nothing left open.`; otherwise unchanged (`needs_you`, `Reached the limit of <n> turns. You can let it continue for a few more.` and `Reached the <m>-minute time limit. You can let it continue for a few more turns.`). A turn that times out after the time limit passed uses the same rule (`Ran out of the <m>-minute time limit during turn <t>` + `.` or `, with your approved file saved and nothing left open.`). "Saved" means a `file_write` action that did not fail and was not undone.
  - Moderator internals (not exported): `resolveAgreement(roomId, proposal)` returns `{ proposalId, fileName, byLabel }` for an agreed file proposal and `null` for a decision proposal; `applyReply(...)` passes that value back; `pauseRoom(state, pause)`; `finish(state, status, reason, { pausedFor, clockUsedMs })`; `limitReached(room, state, decision)`.
  - Agent prompt copy: the two rule sentences now say the room pauses and asks the user and a file is saved only if the user approves it.
  - Test fixtures used again by Task A2: `PAUSING_SCRIPT` (Hermes proposes `plan.md` on turn 1, OpenClaw agrees on turn 2, later turns are plain notes).

- One run of the file takes about 20 to 40 seconds.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the new D10 tests (section 4b).** Insert the following block immediately before the banner comment `// 5. The HTTP router (in-process; ...` (that is, before the line of `=` characters that starts section 5, currently line 1235). It adds the `PAUSING_SCRIPT` fixture and these tests: agreement alone never writes (gate on and off), a decision proposal does not pause, the clock stops while paused, the end rule (five cases), the time-limit end rule, **Review Focus 1: restart while paused**, new-room defaults, and the prompt copy.

````js
// ===========================================================================
// 4b. D10: the Team Room asks first (agreement never writes; the room pauses)
// ===========================================================================

// Hermes proposes plan.md on turn 1 and OpenClaw agrees on turn 2, so the room
// pauses. Any later turn (after Approve, Reject or Continue) is a plain note.
const PAUSING_SCRIPT = {
  hermes: [{ text: fileReply("plan.md", "# Party plan\n- cake") }, { text: "NOTE: after the decision, Hermes" }],
  openclaw: [{ text: "Looks good to me.\nAGREE: P1" }, { text: "NOTE: after the decision, OpenClaw" }]
};

test(
  "D10: agreement alone never writes a file; the room pauses as needs_you with pausedFor set (gate on and gate off)",
  SKIP_POSIX,
  async () => {
    for (const gate of [true, false]) {
      await setScript(PAUSING_SCRIPT);
      await withTeamEnv(
        async (home) => {
          const room = await runRoom("Plan a birthday party", { maxTurns: 6 });
          assert.equal(room.status, "needs_you", `gate ${gate}`);
          assert.equal(room.pausedFor, "P1");
          assert.equal(room.turnsDone, 2);
          assert.equal(room.endReason, "Paused for your decision: Hermes Agent's file plan.md needs your approval.");
          assert.equal(room.currentTurn, null);
          assert.equal(typeof room.clockUsedMs, "number");
          assert.equal(await exists(teamFile(home, room.id, "plan.md")), false);
          const decision = await readDecision(room.id);
          assert.equal(decision.proposals[0].status, "needs_approval");
          assert.equal(decision.proposals[0].statusReason, "Both agents agree. Waiting for your approval.");
          assert.deepEqual(decision.actions, []);
          const events = await readEvents(room.id);
          assert.ok(!events.some((e) => e.type === "action"), "no file action");
          const last = events.at(-1);
          assert.equal(last.type, "status");
          assert.equal(last.status, "needs_you");
          assert.equal(last.pausedFor, "P1");
          assert.match(last.reason, /^Paused for your decision/);
        },
        { gate }
      );
    }
  }
);

test(
  "D10: the clock stops while paused: clockUsedMs keeps the time used, and time passing while paused is not counted",
  SKIP_POSIX,
  async () => {
    await setScript(PAUSING_SCRIPT);
    await withTeamEnv(async () => {
      let offsetMs = 0;
      const moderator = createModerator({ now: () => Date.now() + offsetMs });
      const { room: started, done } = await moderator.startRoom({ task: "slow talk", limits: { maxTurns: 6, maxMinutes: 1 } });
      const unsubscribe = subscribeRoom(started.id, (event) => {
        if (event.type === "turn_ended" && event.turn === 1) offsetMs += 40 * 1000;
        if (event.type === "turn_ended" && event.turn === 2) offsetMs += 10 * 1000;
      });
      await done;
      unsubscribe();
      const paused = await readRoom(started.id);
      assert.equal(paused.status, "needs_you");
      assert.equal(paused.pausedFor, "P1");
      // 50 seconds of fake time plus the few real seconds the two fake turns took.
      assert.ok(paused.clockUsedMs >= 50000 && paused.clockUsedMs < 58000, `clockUsedMs was ${paused.clockUsedMs}`);

      // Ten minutes pass while the room waits for the person: nothing is used up.
      offsetMs += 10 * 60 * 1000;
      const later = await readRoom(started.id);
      assert.equal(later.status, "needs_you");
      assert.equal(later.clockUsedMs, paused.clockUsedMs);
    });
  }
);

test(
  "D10: a room ends agreed only at its limit with an approved file saved and nothing open; otherwise needs_you",
  SKIP_POSIX,
  async () => {
    await withTeamEnv(async () => {
      // Each case pauses at turn 2 (turn limit 2), then Continue adds turns. applyFileProposal is what Approve calls.
      async function pausedRoom(script, task, moderator) {
        await setScript(script);
        const room = await runRoom(task, { maxTurns: 2 }, moderator);
        assert.equal(room.pausedFor, "P1", task);
        return room;
      }
      async function continueAndWait(moderator, roomId, extra) {
        const { done } = await moderator.continueRoom(roomId, extra);
        await done;
        return readRoom(roomId);
      }

      // A. Approved and saved, nothing open: agreed at the limit. The old early exit is gone:
      // turns 3 and 4 are still played after the file was saved.
      let moderator = createModerator();
      let room = await pausedRoom(PAUSING_SCRIPT, "A: approved", moderator);
      await applyFileProposal(room.id, "P1");
      room = await continueAndWait(moderator, room.id, 2);
      assert.equal(room.status, "agreed");
      assert.equal(room.turnsDone, 4);
      assert.equal(room.endReason, "Reached the limit of 4 turns with your approved file saved and nothing left open.");
      assert.equal(room.pausedFor, null);

      // B. Never approved: the card still waits, so it ends needs_you.
      moderator = createModerator();
      room = await pausedRoom(PAUSING_SCRIPT, "B: not approved", moderator);
      room = await continueAndWait(moderator, room.id, 1);
      assert.equal(room.status, "needs_you");
      assert.equal(room.endReason, "Reached the limit of 3 turns. You can let it continue for a few more.");
      assert.equal((await readDecision(room.id)).proposals[0].status, "needs_approval");

      // C. Approved and saved, but another proposal is still open: needs_you.
      const withOpen = {
        hermes: [{ text: fileReply("plan.md", "# Party plan\n- cake") }, { text: "PROPOSE: hire a clown" }, { text: "NOTE: h" }],
        openclaw: [{ text: "Looks good to me.\nAGREE: P1" }, { text: "NOTE: o" }]
      };
      moderator = createModerator();
      room = await pausedRoom(withOpen, "C: open proposal", moderator);
      await applyFileProposal(room.id, "P1");
      room = await continueAndWait(moderator, room.id, 2);
      assert.equal((await readDecision(room.id)).proposals[1].status, "open");
      assert.equal(room.status, "needs_you");

      // D. Approved and saved, but another card waits for approval: needs_you.
      const withCard = {
        hermes: [{ text: fileReply("plan.md", "# Party plan\n- cake") }, { text: "PROPOSE: hire a clown" }, { text: "NOTE: h" }],
        openclaw: [{ text: "Looks good to me.\nAGREE: P1" }, { text: "AGREE: P2" }, { text: "NOTE: o" }]
      };
      moderator = createModerator();
      room = await pausedRoom(withCard, "D: card waits", moderator);
      await applyFileProposal(room.id, "P1");
      room = await continueAndWait(moderator, room.id, 3);
      assert.equal((await readDecision(room.id)).proposals[1].status, "needs_approval");
      assert.equal(room.status, "needs_you");
      assert.equal(room.pausedFor, null, "a decision card never pauses the room");

      // E. The saved file was undone: nothing is saved any more, so needs_you.
      moderator = createModerator();
      room = await pausedRoom(PAUSING_SCRIPT, "E: undone", moderator);
      await applyFileProposal(room.id, "P1");
      await undoAction(room.id, "A1");
      room = await continueAndWait(moderator, room.id, 2);
      assert.equal(room.status, "needs_you");
    });
  }
);

test(
````
